newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mainly firmer, spot month sags.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mainly firmer, spot month sags.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in dull, rangebound dealings Tuesday, as speculative buying was offset by trade selling, floor sources said.
With turnover estimated at only 4,325 lots today, traders said interest in the market was dwindling ahead of the long holiday weekend.
The CSCE will be closed Thursday, November 28 and Friday, November 29, for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Benchmark March coffee settled 0.50 cent a lb firmer, at 108.10, after ranging between 108.75 and 107.50. Spot December futures finished 0.60 cent lower at 117.15, while the remaining months closed up 0.50 to 1.15.
Technically, traders said March resistance was seen near 110.20 cents, while support was pegged at 106.40 cents.
Although a world production report released Tuesday by FO Licht was seen neutral to slightly bullish, dealers said the data had little impact on prices.
"It really had no effect on the market," one trader said. "It seemed as if it was already absorbed into prices."

Licht's first estimate of world production pegged world coffee production at 96.45 million 60-kg bags in the 1996/97 crop year compared with 87.64 million in 1995/96. Although no consumption data was published, they said the increased 1996/97 crop was likely to be lower than world demand.

In other news, the CSCE reported Monday that U.S. certified coffee stocks were unchanged at 321 60-kg bags in the week ended Nov. 22, the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking stocks in 1980. No coffee was pending grading, they said.
